tasks.question: What do you think about people spending so much time on social media?

cues.cue: social media / do / more harm than good
models: In my opinion, social media does more harm than good, because it damages real-world relationships, and this is particularly evident when people prioritise online validation.
Personally, I think that constant scrolling wastes valuable time, because it distracts people from meaningful activities, which means productivity suffers.
It seems to me that social media fuels anxiety, mainly because it encourages constant comparison, and this affects mental health.
I would argue that excessive use erodes attention spans, on the grounds that constant notifications fragment focus, and this weakens concentration over time.

cues.cue: young people / spend / too much time online
models: In my view, young people spend far too much time online, this is mainly because platforms are designed to be addictive, and it is clear that limits are needed.

cues.cue: social media / offer / some genuine benefits
models: My personal opinion is that social media offers some genuine benefits, largely because it keeps people connected across distances, and this should not be overlooked.

tasks.question: What is your view on studying abroad?

models: I believe that studying abroad is worth the cost, because the experience broadens perspectives significantly, and I think this is supported by the skills graduates gain.
From my perspective, living abroad builds independence, it seems clear that students grow more self-reliant, since they must manage daily life alone.

cues.trigger: as far as I am concerned
models: As far as I am concerned, studying abroad opens career doors, the key issue is international exposure, and this is because employers value global experience.
I am of the opinion that cultural immersion deepens language skills, and the main reason for this is that daily practice accelerates fluency far more than classroom study.

cues.cue: the expense / put / many families off
models: In my opinion, the expense puts many families off, because tuition and living costs abroad are considerable, and this is particularly evident when scholarships are unavailable.

cues.cue: studying abroad / suit / some students more than others
models: In my view, studying abroad suits some students more than others, this is mainly because adaptability varies, and it is clear that a period of adjustment is often needed.

tasks.question: What do you think about the way technology is changing our lives?

models: I would argue that technology improves our lives, on the grounds that it saves time on everyday tasks, and this frees people up for other pursuits.

cues.cue: rapid change / leave / some people behind
models: It seems to me that rapid change leaves some people behind, mainly because not everyone can keep pace with new tools, and this creates a digital divide.
Personally, I think that technology reshapes how we communicate, because face-to-face conversation is increasingly replaced by screens, which means relationships feel different.
My personal opinion is that automation threatens traditional jobs, largely because machines now perform tasks once done by people, and this demands new skills.

cues.cue: technology / grant / unprecedented access to information
models: In my opinion, technology grants unprecedented access to information, because anyone with a connection can learn almost anything, and this is particularly evident in remote areas.

cues.cue: constant connectivity / blur / work and leisure
cues.trigger: as far as I am concerned
models: As far as I am concerned, constant connectivity blurs work and leisure, the key issue is the loss of downtime, and this is because devices are always within reach.

tasks.question: What is your opinion on working from home?

cues.cue: working from home / improve / work-life balance
models: In my opinion, working from home improves work-life balance, because employees save time otherwise spent commuting, and this is particularly evident for parents.
I would argue that remote work reduces office collaboration, on the grounds that spontaneous conversations rarely happen online, and this can slow creative problem-solving.
Personally, I think that flexible hours suit many employees, because people can work when they are most productive, which means output often improves.
It seems to me that isolation affects remote workers, mainly because daily social contact disappears, and this can harm mental wellbeing over time.

cues.cue: working from home / demand / strong self-discipline
models: I am of the opinion that working from home demands strong self-discipline, and the main reason for this is that distractions multiply without an office structure.
In my view, companies save considerably on office costs, this is mainly because they need less physical space, and it is clear that many will keep hybrid models.

tasks.question: What do you think about the importance of learning English today?

cues.trigger: as far as I am concerned
models: As far as I am concerned, English is essential today, the key issue is its role as a global language, and this is because it connects speakers of different first languages.
I believe that English opens international career paths, because most global businesses operate in English, and I think this is supported by hiring trends worldwide.

cues.cue: fluency / grant / access to more information online
models: My personal opinion is that fluency grants access to more information online, largely because the majority of web content is written in English, and this shapes what people can learn.
From my perspective, learning English boosts travel confidence, it seems clear that communication becomes far easier, since it is widely spoken worldwide.
I am of the opinion that English dominates academic publishing, and the main reason for this is that most research journals require it, which limits access for non-speakers.

cues.cue: non-native speakers / gain / a real advantage
models: In my view, non-native speakers gain a real advantage from fluency, this is mainly because it widens their job prospects, and it is clear that demand for English skills keeps growing.

tasks.question: What is your view on the amount of homework students are given?

models: In my opinion, students receive too much homework, because it leaves little time for rest, and this is particularly evident during exam periods.
I would argue that homework reinforces classroom learning, on the grounds that practice consolidates new material, and this helps information stick.
It seems to me that excessive homework causes unnecessary stress, mainly because students already face long school days, and this affects their overall wellbeing.
Personally, I think that homework builds independent study habits, because it teaches students to manage their own time, which means they develop useful discipline.

cues.cue: the balance / need / adjusting for younger students
cues.trigger: as far as I am concerned
models: As far as I am concerned, the balance needs adjusting for younger students, the key issue is age-appropriate workload, and this is because young children need more unstructured time.

cues.cue: homework / vary / too much between schools
models: My personal opinion is that homework varies too much between schools, largely because there is no consistent national guideline, and this creates unequal pressure on students.
